contradicting_evidence: Positive 24h BTC and ETH returns and improving aggregate breadth counter a straightforward downside-continuation forecast.
The mid-alt proxy has 56% advancers and a positive median return of approximately +0.51%, showing pockets of strength despite its negative mean.
Positive 7d and 30d stablecoin supply changes and stronger 30d alt relative performance preserve a recovery alternative, without confirming deployed demand.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: Expect uneven participation: BTC may remain comparatively resilient while weaker alt segments face further retests. Recent breadth improvement allows stabilization, but ETF outflows and weak capitalization transmission make sustained broad upside less well supported than a choppy path. This is not a confirmed breakdown forecast.
falsification_conditions: The selective-retest outlook would weaken if breadth improvement persists through price pullbacks, ETH/BTC strengthens and large-, mid- and small-alt proxy returns become consistently positive alongside renewed spot demand.
The mixed outlook would shift toward DOWN if BTC resilience fails while breadth deteriorates, seller-led spot flow persists and additional settled ETF sessions show outflows.
missing_evidence: Subsequent settled ETF sessions distinguishing a single withdrawal day from persistent outflows.
Repeated ETH/BTC, spot-flow and breadth observations showing whether stabilization survives pullbacks.
Observed demand beyond the available capitalization proxies and confirmation of stablecoin deployment.
supporting_evidence: Latest settled ETF outflows weaken the older positive-flow argument in the structural prior; both cannot be treated as simultaneous current support.
The large-alt proxy has approximately 47% advancers and a -1.19% equal-weight return; the small-alt proxy has 35% advancers and a -0.56% equal-weight return.
Only approximately 18% of large-alt, 32% of mid-alt and 15% of small-alt proxy constituents outperform BTC, indicating weak broad transmission.
Small hourly price and OI declines suggest some leverage reduction, but do not establish that selling is exhausted or that recovery has begun.
